draft.title: Trade under the Mongols
card: The Silk Road was a network of trade routes linking China with Central Asia and lands further west. Merchants carried goods such as silk and spices along it.
Mongol rulers controlled much of the land the Silk Road crossed. Their soldiers patrolled the routes, so travellers faced less danger from bandits and warring states.
The Mongols also ran a relay postal system. Riders passed messages from station to station, changing tired horses for fresh ones, so news and orders travelled fast.
With safer roads, goods, ideas and people moved across Asia. One traveller was Marco Polo, a merchant from Venice, whose later account of his journeys told many Europeans about China.
draft.remember: Mongol rule made travel across Asia safer and faster, so trade, ideas and travellers could move.

a.q: How did the Mongol relay postal system help the empire?
opts: Riders changed horses at stations, so messages moved fast
Merchants paid riders to carry their silk across Asia
Soldiers at each station guarded the roads from bandits
Riders carried messages by one horse over the whole route
a.why: Stations let riders swap tired horses for fresh ones, so news and orders crossed the empire quickly. Guarding the roads helped travellers, but the card gives that job to soldiers patrolling the routes, not to the postal system.
a.clue: Think about what happened at each station.

b.q: Leila, a merchant, travels from Persia to China in the 1260s with a caravan of goods. Why is her journey safer than it would have been before Mongol rule?
opts: Mongol soldiers patrolled the routes she travelled
Mongol rulers gave her caravan free goods to sell
The Silk Road was shorter after the Mongols arrived
Mongol rulers banned all other merchants from the roads
b.why: Mongol control of the land meant soldiers patrolled the routes, so there was less danger from bandits and warring states. Nothing on the card says the Mongols shortened the road. It was made safer, not shorter.
b.clue: Think about who watched over the roads.

a.best: Riders changed horses at stations, so messages moved fast

b.best: Mongol soldiers patrolled the routes she travelled
